_comment: Which boards belong to which robot, for the front end.
A manifest rather than a naming convention, because a robot's boards do not
reliably share a prefix — the rover's controller run is called 'regress' and the
CAD side will add its own names on its own schedule. Anything not listed here
falls back to prefix grouping and then to 'unassigned', so adding a run never
'role' is what the board does in the robot; 'count' is how many are fitted, which
is how one verified design becomes two motor drivers.

robots.name: Tendon-driven hand
robots.description: Three boards: a palm controller, a five-channel servo driver, and one tactile sensor per fingertip (five fitted).

boards.note: STM32F103 + 3V3 regulation; five PWM out, five analog in
five 3-pin servo headers, bulk for five servos starting together
FSR divider buffered by a unity-gain follower — one per finger

robots.name: 4-wheel rover
robots.description: Four boards: power distribution, two identical motor drivers, a controller, and a status indicator.

boards.note: 2S LiPo in, reverse protection, bulk, fan-out
DRV8833 dual H-bridge, one board per side

robots.name: Bench and fixtures
robots.description: Boards used to exercise the pipeline rather than to fly on a robot.

boards.note: the rover with a manufacturable via stack — every gate green
smallest board that exercises the from-spec path

robots.name: AI-generated
robots.description: Boards the model designed from a written specification, rather than seeded HDL.

boards.note: spec -> parts plan -> HDL -> gates, generated by qwen3.8-27b
